clue.text: Sack England's opener after key game

parts.note: a key is a literal translation used by students, also called a crib
a sack is a bag

indicators.note: an opener is the first letter of the word it belongs to

explanation.surface: Someone is fired after England's opening batsman fails in a crucial match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is a placing indicator: the sack and England's first letter come after the key. A crib, meaning a key, is a student's translation aid.
explanation.definitionFit: Cribbage is a card game scored by moving pegs on a board.

clue.text: Players given the French pieces for chess board

parts.note: the cast is the set of players in a show
les is French for the (plural)

explanation.surface: Actors are given French chessmen to play with.
explanation.definitionFit: Castles, also called rooks, are pieces used in chess.

clue.text: Outrage when republic loses land

indicators.note: loses means the land word is taken away from the republic

parts.note: Ireland is a republic
taken as written

explanation.surface: There is anger when a country surrenders territory.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is anger, the feeling of outrage.

clue.text: Sponsor school wanting half-day for game

parts.note: to sponsor something is to back it
a gam is a school of whales

indicators.note: half means only the first three letters of the day are used

parts.note: Monday is a day of the week

explanation.surface: A school short of a half-day seeks a sponsor for a sports event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes MON, the first half of MONDAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Backgammon is a board game played with dice and counters.

clue.text: Transfixed, show sign of embarrassment

definitions.meaning: pierced through, as by a bull's horns

explanation.surface: Someone frozen to the spot blushes with embarrassment.
explanation.definitionFit: Gored means pierced by a horn; split as go red it means to blush.

clue.text: Clobber and rubbish outside hospital

indicators.note: outside means the rubbish word goes round the hospital letter

parts.note: rubbish is trash
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital on maps and signs

explanation.surface: Someone is beaten up next to piles of rubbish outside a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: To clobber someone is to beat them soundly, a synonym of thrash.

clue.text: Bumpkin, dim, wasting time

indicators.note: wasting means the time letter is lost from the word for dim

parts.note: dim and thick both mean stupid

explanation.surface: A slow-witted country fellow idles away the hours.
explanation.definitionFit: A hick is an unsophisticated rural person, a synonym of bumpkin.

clue.text: Notice vehicle with building material making progress

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
a van is a vehicle
cement is a building material

explanation.surface: A lorry carrying cement makes headway, according to an advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: Advancement is forward movement or promotion, a synonym of progress.

clue.text: Last offer

definitions.meaning: to endure or resist, as a besieged town does
to hold something out to someone is to offer it

explanation.definitionFit: To hold out is to last under siege, and also to extend something as an offer.

clue.text: Reconditioned devices somehow made right inside

indicators.note: inside means the right letter sits within the rearranged letters
somehow says the letters of devices are to be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Faulty gadgets were repaired internally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges DEVICES and 'inside' puts R within them.
explanation.definitionFit: A serviced machine has been overhauled, which is what reconditioned means.

clue.text: Conservative plan — persevere somehow to install Conservative PM

indicators.note: to install means to put the second Conservative letter inside the rearranged letters
somehow says the letters of these words are to be arranged in some new way

parts.note: C again abbreviates Conservative
C again abbreviates Conservative

explanation.surface: A Tory strategy is to keep going until a Conservative leader is placed in office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges the first Conservative with the two plain words; 'to install' puts the second C inside. Perceval, a Tory, was the only British Prime Minister to be assassinated (1812).
explanation.definitionFit: Spencer Perceval was Prime Minister of Britain from 1809 until his murder in 1812.

clue.text: Rider who gave up the usual habit?

definitions.text: Rider who gave up the usual habit?

parts.words: Rider who gave up the usual habit?
parts.note: a habit is both riding dress and clothing in general; the legendary rider through Coventry wore nothing at all

explanation.surface: A horsewoman abandons her customary riding outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend says this noblewoman rode naked through Coventry to protest her husband's taxes, so she gave up clothes, the usual habit, altogether.
explanation.definitionFit: The legend tells of a noblewoman riding through Coventry with no clothing at all.

clue.text: Appointment with examiner for which the right gear is essential

definitions.text: Appointment with examiner for which the right gear is essential

parts.words: Appointment with examiner for which the right gear is essential
parts.note: it suggests a medical or exam needing the proper kit; the gear is the gearbox of a car, and the examiner is a motoring assessor

explanation.surface: Someone must wear the correct outfit to see an examiner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gear' looks like clothing; it is the car's gear, which a learner must select correctly.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate meets an examiner and must change gear correctly to pass this motoring exam.

clue.text: Wreck multinational party?

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, is a multinational body
a do is a party in informal British usage

explanation.surface: A party thrown by an international organisation is ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo something, as in undoing someone's work, is to ruin or wreck it.

clue.text: Super sport excited fans

indicators.note: excited suggests the letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: Enthusiasts are thrilled by a great sporting contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporters of a team are its fans.

clue.text: In loss of control, Mrs French aquaplaned, perhaps

indicators.note: In places the French title inside the word for a loss of control

parts.note: a skid is a loss of control of a vehicle
Mme, for Madame, is the French equivalent of Mrs

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman loses control of her car and slides on a wet road.
explanation.definitionFit: A car that aquaplanes skims over water on the road surface, an example of skimming.

clue.text: Sweetie admits deceptive act in church office

indicators.note: admits means the sweetie word lets the deceptive act inside it

parts.note: deary is a term of endearment like sweetie
a con is a deceptive trick

explanation.surface: A loved one confesses to a fraud in a church post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admits' looks like confessing; it means letting CON into DEARY.
explanation.definitionFit: A deaconry is the office or position of a deacon in the church.

clue.text: Most basic livelihood involving the lowest classes of society

indicators.note: involving means the livelihood word wraps round the class letters

parts.note: a crust, as in earning a crust, is a livelihood
D and E are the lowest grades in the British social classification of occupations

explanation.surface: The poorest people have the barest means of earning a living.
explanation.walkthrough: British market research grades society A, B, C1, C2, D, E, so D and E are the lowest classes.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude means rough and basic, so the most basic is the crudest.

clue.text: State briefly represented by extreme characters

definitions.text: State briefly represented by extreme characters

parts.words: State briefly represented by extreme characters
parts.note: a US state whose short postal code is AZ, the very first and very last letters of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A nation's name is shortened to just its outermost letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' points to the state's abbreviation, and the extreme characters of the alphabet are A and Z.
explanation.definitionFit: The south-western US state's postal abbreviation is AZ, the alphabet's first and final letters.

clue.text: One who helps a person playing the lottery?

definitions.meaning: someone who aids or assists, usually in wrongdoing
someone who places a bet, a gambler

explanation.definitionFit: An abetter assists someone; split as a better it is someone who gambles.

clue.text: Spend penny — allowed to go into river!

indicators.note: to go into means the penny and allowed letters are placed inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in England, Wales and Scotland
let means allowed

explanation.surface: Someone is told to spend a penny, that is relieve themselves, in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spend a penny' is a British euphemism for using the lavatory, which colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To deplete a supply is to use it up or spend it.

clue.text: Intrepid leader coming out like Vincent, late in life?

indicators.note: leader is the first letter, and coming out means it is removed

parts.note: intrepid means fearless

explanation.surface: A brave leader emerges, resembling an elderly painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Vincent van Gogh cut off part of his ear in 1888, two years before he died.
explanation.definitionFit: Van Gogh notoriously cut off his ear, so late in life he was without one.

clue.text: Side's marginal advantage

definitions.meaning: a side of something is its ... or border
having the ... on someone is a slight advantage

explanation.definitionFit: An edge is both the border of an object and a narrow lead over a rival.

clue.text: Lay worker?

parts.note: lay here is a noun meaning a song or ballad, so a worker on lays writes them; it pretends to be a non-clergy church helper

explanation.surface: A member of the church laity helps out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay' looks like the adjective for non-clergy; it is the old word for a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A lay is a song, so a lay worker is someone who composes songs.

clue.text: Boss not right, making embarrassing mistake

indicators.note: not means the right letter is left out of the boss word

parts.note: gaffer is British slang for a boss

explanation.surface: A boss who is in the wrong commits a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffe is a social blunder that causes embarrassment.

clue.text: Manage to seize illegal drug

parts.note: to cop is slang for to seize or catch
E is slang for ecstasy, an illegal drug

explanation.surface: Someone manages to get hold of illicit drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words mean handling a difficulty successfully and getting by.

clue.text: Desolate city region for Othello?

parts.note: read as a barren upland belonging to an Italian canal city, it is also the full subtitle of Shakespeare's tragedy about the general

explanation.surface: A bleak urban area is set aside for a famous general.
explanation.walkthrough: A moor is desolate open land, so the clue reads as a wild part of Venice; Othello is a Moor, and the play's full title is Othello, the Moor of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's play is titled Othello, the Moor of Venice, naming its North African general.

clue.text: Local home on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means as heard in a broadcast

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A local station broadcasts from someone's house.
explanation.walkthrough: A local is British slang for one's nearest pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A local, in British English, is a nearby pub, which an inn is.

clue.text: Pretty despicable character, that woman

parts.note: a rat is a despicable person
her refers to that woman

explanation.surface: A rather nasty woman is described.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretty and rather both mean fairly or somewhat, as in pretty good.

clue.text: Poor people producing vegetables, hill-workers?

parts.note: peas are vegetables
worker ants live in anthills

explanation.surface: Impoverished smallholders grow vegetables and labour on the hillsides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hill workers' suggests farm labourers on slopes; it means the insects of an anthill.
explanation.definitionFit: Peasants are poor agricultural labourers, the poor people of rural society.
